subject: technology
essential_question: What can this data honestly support, and what would make the conclusion wrong?
standards: Michigan Computer Science: Data and Analysis
project_brief: Produce a reproducible data analysis with provenance, uncertainty, stated limitations, and an honest visualization set. This is the grade 11 culminating project for "Applied Data Science and Modeling" (ma-g11-technology-u04, unit 4), built around question framing and study design, acquisition cleaning and provenance, exploratory analysis, visualization integrity, and correlation causation and uncertainty. Collect or use a small, fictional or already-approved data set related to question framing and study design, acquisition cleaning and provenance, exploratory analysis, and visualization integrity, and turn it into a labeled visual with a one-paragraph, evidence-based conclusion.
requirements: Address every topic listed for this unit: question framing and study design, acquisition cleaning and provenance, exploratory analysis, visualization integrity, correlation causation and uncertainty, and reproducible reporting.
Meet the performance task as written: Produce a reproducible data analysis with provenance, uncertainty, stated limitations, and an honest visualization set.
Show your work or process, not just a final result — a process note, sketch log, commit history, or draft trail.
Complete the checklist in this package before submitting.
primary_task: Collect or use a small, fictional or already-approved data set related to question framing and study design, acquisition cleaning and provenance, exploratory analysis, and visualization integrity, and turn it into a labeled visual with a one-paragraph, evidence-based conclusion.
test_or_check_criteria: Every claim or design choice in the submission can be traced to question framing and study design or another named topic from this unit — nothing is left unexplained.
The submission runs, displays, or demonstrates correctly on at least two different sample inputs or scenarios the student chooses.
No real password, API key, account credential, precise location, or other real personal/system data appears anywhere in the submission — fictional or sandbox examples only.
The student can explain, in their own words, why each step or decision was made, not just that it works.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: This project never touches a real account, a real password or API key, a live production system, or another person's real data. Use fictional names, sandbox environments, local files, or already-approved sample data throughout. Submit code, screenshots of your own sandbox, diagrams, or a written walkthrough — a live public deployment is never required.

copyright_and_authorship: The final submitted work must remain your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI assistant may help you plan, explain a concept, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but may not produce the graded work itself. Never request, store, or submit a real password, API key, access token, or other real credential; use only fictional accounts and sandboxed or offline systems.
remediation: If the project stalls, step back to the smallest version of the task: rebuild just the part covering question framing and study design in isolation, using a worked example from this unit as a model, then re-attach it to the full project once that smaller piece works and you can explain why.
extension: Once the core project is working, extend it to handle a new constraint or edge case related to acquisition cleaning and provenance, or compare two different approaches to the same problem and explain the real tradeoff between them in your own words.
